What I changed
- Direct weight edits (MLP down_proj column scaling), two complementary mechanisms, all in `/work/edited`:
  1. Eleven "Wait-loop" writer columns zeroed: (layer, unit) = (23,168), (20,1111), (16,2241), (18,133), (19,927), (15,2913), (5,462), (22,616), (18,258), (16,120), (15,2540).
  2. Eight "close-the-thinking-block" writer columns doubled: (19,31), (18,2066), (23,576), (19,893), (16,172), (23,163), (22,777), (23,872).

Why — the failure mechanism I found
- In ~92-95% of original-weight generations on practice problems, the model never closes its `<think>` section: it enters a self-reinforcing "Wait, ..." loop (identical 1-2-sentence repeats, e.g. "Wait, is it possible that 'primary grades' refers to the *middle school*?" ×20; "* I will write the response." ×30+) and hits the 8192-token cap. Completions were almost always correct (7/7 in one diagnostic batch), and cut texts almost never produced a boxed answer, so the whole failure is "thinking never terminates," not reasoning per-step.
- Teacher-forced passes (mlp_act + hidden states decomposition) showed: (a) a consistent set of MLP units across three independent loop fragments correlates with predicting " Wait" (corr 0.4-0.74 across fragments) and writes toward the Wait unembedding direction; zeroing those columns fixes GSM repetition (confirm: +7-10pp on untouched GSM problems) but not MATH; (b) a separate set of units fires essentially only at the position where a finished correct solution emits `</think>` (z>2.3 vs own-text baseline; negligible activation elsewhere and in loop regions), writes toward the `</think>` (248069) unembedding readout, and is ~orthogonal to the Wait readout. Doubling their down_proj columns makes the model close thinking once the solution is formed instead of wallowing. Final-norm formula verified numerically (Qwen3.5 uses (1+γ) scaling).

Measured effect (paired "both" passes, identical seeds)
- MATH-500-style practice: on 314 untouched confirm generations (never used to pick anything), accuracy 29/314 → 50/314, +6.69pp, McNemar-style SE 2.14pp, gain/SE ≈ 3.1; 33 problems went wrong→right, 12 right→wrong. (Without the close-amplification only, MATH gain was a null 0-1.45pp; amplification x3 was worse, x2 better than x1.5.)
- GSM confirm (untouched): +7.07pp ± 2.38pp (19 wrong→right, 5 right→wrong); earlier GSM confirms +9.78pp/+3.64pp.
- Shorter-but-closing generations are not rushed junk: short-close samples were predominantly correct, and right→wrong flips were rare.
- Scope note: edits touch only MLP down_proj matrices. The MATH-specific loop is heterogeneous (problem-specific repeated sentences), so gains are real but modest; the edit does not touch the final norm, embeddings, attention, vision tower, or whole tensors, and is not a global distribution knob.
